audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty text never names a Sylas ability and the level chart disagrees between layers.
audit.why: Sylas's lane threat is one 400-range dash (Abscond, 13/12/11/10/9s) plus Kingslayer sustain; the difficulty is entirely about that one cooldown, not a generic all-in.
audit.corrected: Early lane is his because Abscond closes 400 units and Kingslayer (W, 12s at rank 1) heals the trade back; post-6 Glacial Storm inverts it.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and wants.you[2] call Sylas's ultimate 'Hextech Flashtraption'.
audit.why: Sylas's R is Hijack (80/55/30s), which steals the enemy ultimate. Hextech Flashtraption is a rune. Worse, the thing Hijack most wants here is YOUR Glacial Storm.
audit.corrected: Hijack (R) named, and the real spike interaction stated: he can steal Glacial Storm off you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Abilities referred to only as 'Abscond / Abduct' with no cooldowns, and the Crystallize/dash interaction is never stated.
audit.why: Crystallize (W, 17s) is terrain — it denies the Abscond dash and leaves Abduct with nothing to pull to. Flash Frost chill makes Frostbite double damage. Kingslayer is a heal, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades (flagged in missingInteractions).
audit.corrected: Wall the dash lane, Q for the chill, E for double damage; buy anti-heal into Kingslayer.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3..6].side did not match win[3..6] or packet.levelChart.
audit.why: Four of seven rows rendered two different answers to 'who wins this stage'.
audit.corrected: Full layer aligned to the content layer and the packet chart.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - W Crystallize is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Abscond (E) is his only gap-closer: 13s at rank 1, and Abduct can only recast off that dash. Step up while it is down. - Crystallize (17s) is your Flash — hold it for his E line. - Hijack steals YOUR Glacial Storm.

edits.before: Sylas wins by landing Abscond / Abduct, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Sylas wins by dashing past Q with Abscond, healing the trade back on Kingslayer, then stealing your Glacial Storm.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Sylas burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Wait for him to spend Abscond, wall the landing spot, then Q for the stun and E for double damage — Kingslayer heals nothing he never lands.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Sylas walks straight at you.
edits.after: Spending Q on the wave while Abscond is up — no stun threat means he walks in, heals off Kingslayer, and leaves.

edits.before: Good trade: Threaten Q until Sylas burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade. Bad trade: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Sylas walks straight at you.
edits.after: Good trade: Wait for him to spend Abscond, wall the landing spot, then Q for the stun and E for double damage — Kingslayer heals nothing he never lands. Bad trade: Spending Q on the wave while Abscond is up — no stun threat means he walks in, heals off Kingslayer, and leaves.

edits.before: If Sylas takes first blood, tighten up: Abscond / Abduct is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with R wave-clear and stay relevant through zone control.
edits.after: If Sylas takes first blood, Kingslayer heals him back to full off your wave — buy Oblivion Orb early and stop funding it. A second kill ends the duel, not the game: R-clear from range and win on zone control.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by denying a 400-range dash: put Crystallize between Sylas and your carries and Abduct has nothing left to pull him to.

edits.before: Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: A short wave keeps you outside Abscond's 400 range, so his 13s dash has to cross open ground to reach you.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Sylas burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Crystallize is terrain: dropped on his Abscond line it deletes the dash, and Abduct has no target left to chain him back out with.

edits.before: Sylas whiffs Abscond / Abduct and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Abscond spent inbound means no dash out — Q, E and turret finish it.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Sylas walks straight at you.
edits.after: His minions feed Petricite Burst charges and Kingslayer heals off every one — you chase into a full-health Sylas.

edits.before: Sylas's Q-E dash-and-chain combo lets him close the gap on your immobile kit and punish any Egg cooldown before level 6.
edits.after: Abscond (E) in, Abduct back on you, Kingslayer (W) heals the trade back — his 13s E cooldown is the only safe window you get.

edits.before: Glacial Storm gives you the zone and slow to answer his all-in, and if he doesn't have a strong ult to steal, his Hextech Flashtraption loses a lot of value against you.
edits.after: Glacial Storm gives you the zone and slow to answer his all-in — but Hijack (R) steals it, so hold the storm until his E is spent and he cannot follow you into your own zone.

edits.before: Track enemy ults he could steal with Hextech Flashtraption before committing your own
edits.after: Track what Hijack (R) can steal — your own Glacial Storm included — before committing

edits.before: Same story at level 4 — his all-in threat outpaces your trading potential.
edits.after: Level 3 arms Abscond — a 13s dash against your 17s wall, so he closes more often.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 remain his window since his combo and healing passive still outvalue your poke.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his: Kingslayer (W) heals your poke back and Chain Lash outranges you at 775.
